title: Edge failover debug scratchpad
content:
Context: quick personal notes on the 2026-02-18/19 regional failover where routing policy fell back to eu-west despite healthy us-west capacity. This is a messy scratchpad — commands run, raw errors, hypotheses, and next steps.

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-18 22:40 UTC: Customer reports spikes in tail latency for requests routed to us-west; spike correlates with a deployment burst.
- 2026-02-18 22:45 UTC: Automated smart routing policy triggered fallback to next region (eu-west) for a subset of traffic — unexpected for us-west (should be fallback to us-central).
- 2026-02-18 22:48–23:10 UTC: Mixed routing: some requests still try us-west, others routed to eu-west; client observed increased p99.
- 2026-02-19 01:12 UTC: Rollback of the candidate runtime kernel on us-west. Traffic gradually returned, but TTL of cache keys caused some sessions to remain routed to eu-west for ~30 minutes.

Commands I ran (local shell + k8s + curl):
- Check routing config in console v2 API: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://console.internal.redwood/api/v2/routing/policies?region=us-west" | jq '.'
- Dump current policy revision: curl -s https://console.internal.redwood/api/v2/routing/policies/us-west/revision | jq '.revision, .rules[]'
- Verify service endpoints: kubectl -n inference get endpoints router-us-west -o yaml
- Inspect router logs (tail): kubectl -n inference logs deploy/router-us-west --since=2h | egrep "fallback|route decision|cache miss" > /tmp/router-us-west-tail.log
- Replayed request with header forcing region: curl -H 'X-Region-Hint: us-west' -v https://api.redwood/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'

Snippets from logs (redacted):
- [2026-02-18T22:46:11Z] router-us-west decision=FALLBACK reason=capacity_estimate_unavailable score=NaN 
- [2026-02-18T22:46:11Z] router-us-west chosen_target=eu-west weights=[us-west:0.0, eu-west:1.0, us-central:0.0]
- [2026-02-18T22:46:11Z] cache: prefix_kv hit=false key=convo:abc123 ttl=0 (stale)
- [2026-02-18T22:47:02Z] autoscaler: scale_event detected candidate_kernel_deploy=optim_v3 id=deploy-289 status=partial-failure

Hypotheses (brainstorming):
1) Score computation bug: capacity_estimate was computed earlier in pipeline; an upstream NaN bubbled up and policy evaluation treated NaN as lowest score -> forced regional switch to eu-west.
   - Evidence: explicit score=NaN in router logs.
   - Check: trace upstream metric calculations (metrics service /metrics/capacity/us-west) for NaNs around 22:45 UTC.
2) Policy precedence mismatch: policy ordering for fallbacks may be using alphabetical region sort somewhere, and when a target score equals 0 it picks first non-zero? But logs show us-central=0 and eu-west chosen; alphabetical wouldn't pick eu-west necessarily.
3) KV cache staleness drove incorrect session affinity -> router saw many cache misses and treated session as new, then applied global fallback list (eu-west top of list for that tenant).
4) Partial kernel deploy left some capacity rows in an indeterminate state (autoscaler reported partial-failure). The capacity API returned 503 for a short window and our router treats 5xx as capacity_unavailable and picks hard-coded first fallback.

Things I tried and results: 
- Replayed single request locally with X-Region-Hint -> server respected hint and routed to us-west when the hint header present. Means header precedence path is okay.
- Queried capacity API during incident window (from logs) -> returned 503 then 200. Snapshot: 503 at 22:46:09, 200 at 22:48:30.
- Reproduced NaN in local unit test by dividing zero capacity into utilization metric; found a code path in metrics-aggregator where we compute pct = requests / capacity and we don't guard capacity==0 -> results in Infinity/NaN after float casts.

Quick root-cause working theory: autoscaler half-applied a kernel rollout causing ephemeral 0 capacity rows for some worker pools; metrics-aggregator computed pct = requests/capacity then emitted NaN which propagated to routing service. Routing eval treats NaN as minimal and defaulted to tenant fallback list which had eu-west first for that tenant (weird ordering from a recent change).

Immediate mitigations (notes to self):
- Add guard in metrics-aggregator: if capacity <= 0 then emit capacity_available=false metric and set pct=0 (dont emit NaN). Quick patch: PR against metrics-aggregator.
- Change routing evaluation to treat NaN explicitly as 'unavailable' and consult fallback precedence that prefers same-continent or same-cloud first (policy change).
- Add canary check for partial-deploy: autoscaler should not flip capacity rows to 0 until rollout confirmed; add a pre-commit safety flag.

Followups / TODOs: 
- [ ] File INC-4521 notes + link logs (done, but expand with these snippets).
- [ ] PR: metrics-aggregator NaN guard (prepare, test, quick-release). Owner: me (Asha).
- [ ] PR: router eval NaN handling + explicit fallback-order enforcement (owner: Riley).
- [ ] Improve observability: dashboard that shows NaN counts from aggregator -> route-decisions graph. (owner: Miguel).
- [ ] Postmortem draft: collect customer impact + SLA footprint. (owner: eng-incident-response).

Questions / open doubts:
- Why did tenant fallback order list eu-west ahead of us-central? There's a recent change in tenant-fallback-service where we changed sort from "latency" to "score"; need to check default for unscored items.
- How many tenants had eu-west as first fallback? If this is a lot, the customer impact surface increases. Quick query: SELECT count(tenant) FROM tenant_fallbacks WHERE fallback[0] = 'eu-west' 
- Is there any client-side sticky affinity that would have preserved sessions to us-west even if router switched? Some older SDKs do local sticky -> check customer SDK versions for impacted customers.

Useful pointers to include in postmortem:
- Attach /tmp/router-us-west-tail.log (already pulled).
- Autoscaler events (deploy-289 timeline).
- Metrics-aggregator code snippet showing missing capacity guard (file: metrics/agg/percentile.go lines ~112-128).

Notes to self for PR message: explain NaN -> fallback behavior with minimal repro and logs. Keep the fix small and add unit tests for capacity==0.

Random scratch ideas (maybe overkill):
- Add a small "sanity check" in the control plane that rejects policy eval results with NaN or Infinity and forces explicit unavailable flag.
- Rate-limit fallback changes: if region switches > X per minute for a tenant, don't auto-fallback—alert SRE instead to avoid oscillation.

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into proper incident timeline & postmortem later.

-- Asha
